mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5% median) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for three months, as measured by a one-tailed t-test with p > 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening household demand, which reduces earnings expectations for consumer-facing equities and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1.0% median) when GDPC1 YoY change < -2%, as measured by a one-tailed t-test with p > 0.15.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses wage growth and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5% median) when UNRATE > 4% for two consecutive months, with p > 0.10 in a one-tailed test.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 98 for three consecutive months indicates supply chain stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5% median) when INDPRO < 98 for three months, with p > 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and accelerating inflation, which increases real discount rates and erodes real equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1.0% median) when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages, with p > 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 5% signals a recovery in residential investment, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market sentiment, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5% median) when HOUST monthly change > 5%, with p > 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their 6-month averages indicates robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1.0% median) when both PAYEMS and UNRATE exceed their 6-month moving averages, with p > 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth expectations for retail and related sectors, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1.0% median) when RSAFS < 12-mo MA for four months, with p > 0.10.
